title: Every Large Language Model Explained in 17 Minutes!
description:
👨‍💻 Learn AI Engineering Interactively  With Scrimba With 20% Discount  :  https://scrimba.com/fullstack-path-c0fullstack?via=codist

There are dozens of LLMs out there — GPT, Claude, Gemini, 
Llama, Mistral, Grok, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, and counting. 
They all look similar from the outside, but under the hood 
they're built with completely different trade-offs: some chase 
raw intelligence, some optimize for speed, some are open-weight, 
some are obsessed with long context, and some are quietly 
winning on price.

In this video, I break down every major LLM you actually need 
to know in 2026 — what each one is good at, what it's bad at, 
who built it, and when you should reach for it. By the end, 
you'll stop picking models by vibes and start picking them by 
what the job actually needs.

top_comments.author: @joshuazhao
top_comments.text:
If we can get DeepSeek to run offline, along with Qwen, Kimi, Gemma, you basically get a mixed AI that probably can eventually outsmart Claude Opus.

I don't know if other AI did this yet, but the last time I heard about DeepSeek, is that they don't use traditional training data to train the AI, they use a correctional training routine, if the AI makes a mistake, it will learn from that mistake, and refine the response for next time. So with this, eventually, DeepSeek's reasoning will improve over time, just like how we humans or animals learn from past experiences.

This is why initially, DeepSeek obliterated the AI market and made waves. This is a capability that will eventually make it better and more smarter overtime, the ever evolving AI model.
